heading: Special-purpose industrial furnace procurement
title: Special-purpose furnace procurement: annealing, gas firing, controlled atmospheres, spheroidizing and ovens
description: Compare industrial furnace requirements by workpiece, loading, process and site utilities. Confirm specifications, interfaces and scope of supply for your project.
publisherName: Jiangsu Suneng Industrial Furnace Co., Ltd.

references.title: Gas nitriding furnace design and selection

html:
Suneng can assess enquiries for chamber annealing, gas-fired heat treatment, forging heat, regenerative heating, solution treatment, nitriding, controlled atmospheres, spheroidizing annealing, industrial drying and curing. Describe the material or workpiece, intended result and site conditions before agreeing the equipment design, configuration and scope of quotation.

Terms such as “large” and “rapid”, a load rating, a dimension or a station count do not define a plant design. Confirm the specifications, applicable duty, supply scope and acceptance requirements for the individual project.

Chamber annealing, gas-fired heat treatment, forging and regenerative heating

For electric chamber annealing furnaces, indoor forging heating furnaces, gas-fired heat treatment or regenerative furnaces, provide the material, part dimensions, batch load or continuous cycle, process requirements, handling method and available power or gas supply.

The names “chamber” and “box” alone do not make two furnaces interchangeable. Gas firing or regenerative heating describes only part of the design. Establish the loading arrangement, heating duty and system boundaries before choosing a design. Conditions for heating aluminium before forging cannot be applied directly to other materials.

Solution treatment, nitriding, aluminium alloy quenching and large controlled-atmosphere furnaces

For a rapid solution furnace, large nitriding furnace, aluminium quench furnace or large controlled-atmosphere furnace, identify material and incoming condition, process, quantity, loading and atmosphere requirements. Specify how the product will be tested and how the equipment will be accepted.

Check the handover from solution treatment to quenching, the nitriding route and the controlled-atmosphere configuration separately. Similar names do not establish that the processes can use the same equipment. Determine size, loading, records and site services for the project.

Large bell furnaces

For enquiries described as a 300-tonne twin-base bell furnace or a 5.2-metre bell furnace, supply the original documents and the new project conditions. Establish what the tonnage and dimension refer to, then check the load envelope, base capacity, bell clearance, lifting and handling, process and atmosphere.

These descriptions identify purchase enquiries. They are not standard current ratings or delivery commitments. Review bell furnace design and selection and confirm the actual specification separately.

Industrial ovens, mould preheating and twin-station curing

Specify the material or workpiece, intended use, temperature profile, load, batch pattern and cycle. For curing, also supply the material requirements, station arrangement, exhaust and utility details.

Two stations do not necessarily constitute two independent systems. A continuous gas cylinder curing line is not a substitute for every drying or curing oven. Agree separate acceptance criteria for equipment performance and material or product results.

Spheroidizing annealing equipment

Single-deck continuous, double-deck continuous and pit-type spheroidizing annealing furnaces can be assessed for a specific project. Supply the material, incoming condition, part or coil form, loading arrangement, process basis and target production interval.

Batch and continuous operation, and single- and double-deck arrangements, organise the load differently. Check the actual conveying or loading conditions before selecting the design. A similar equipment name does not establish suitability for your parts or acceptance criteria.

Gas-fired furnaces: match the loading arrangement and application

Specify the material, part shape, batch load or continuous production interval, temperature profile, handling and available gas supply. Assess trolley, pit and chamber arrangements separately. The term “gas furnace” alone does not define structure or supply scope.

For heavy parts or two-trolley operation, see trolley furnaces and heating options. For vertical loading, see pit furnace structure and heat sources. For forging, gas-fired heat treatment or regenerative heating, check application and site conditions.

For mould preheating and twin-station curing, check the procurement requirements for preheating and curing. Confirm material, temperature profile, exhaust and heat source. Neither duty automatically requires gas firing. For replacements, also supply the existing nameplate, drawings and configuration.

Electric resistance furnaces: distinguish structure, heat source and process

Provide workpiece, material, load, temperature profile, handling method, available power and planned cycle. Compare the actual loading method with resistance-heated trolley and twin-trolley arrangements or pit furnace designs and heat sources.

For solution treatment, nitriding, aluminium quenching or controlled atmospheres, check the process and site requirements. The process name alone determines neither the heat source nor whether one furnace can serve several routes. Define heating, processing, handling and downstream operations separately.

Drying furnaces: clarify the material, purpose and exhaust requirements

Provide the material or workpiece, drying objective, known temperature profile, batch load or continuous cycle, handling, material documentation, exhaust and available utilities. For replacement equipment, add the nameplate, photographs, drawings and current service conditions.

Distinguish drying, preheating and curing before confirming whether Suneng can take on the work, the equipment type and the supply scope. Compare industrial oven, mould preheating and twin-station curing requirements. These names do not identify the model, dimensions or configuration of an existing machine.

Continuous stainless steel annealing and pickling: define product form and supply boundaries

First identify whether the product is strip or another form. Provide material, dimensions, incoming and target condition, process data, operating cycle, and an existing layout or equipment list. A line name alone does not determine the conveying arrangement or full configuration.

For strip, compare the thermal section and delivery interfaces of an annealing and solution treatment line. Name the suppliers and interface owners for the furnace, pickling, washing, accumulators, payoff and recoiling. Other product forms and line equipment require separate assessment. A description of the furnace section does not imply supply of the whole pickling line.

What to send with a procurement enquiry

Send the workpiece or material description, equipment name, site photographs, known process requirements and planned output. For replacement equipment or new auxiliaries, include the original manufacturer, model, nameplate and drawings. Identify missing information first. Confirm design, supply, costs and delivery in the project documents.

Contact Suneng about a special-purpose furnace. For continuous annealing or solution treatment, review workpieces and equipment boundaries for the line.
